---
title: Block before you compare
---

## Why blocking is needed

Comparing every record in file A to every record in file B is usually infeasible. Blocking reduces the candidate set by requiring coarse agreement on a few fields before detailed comparison.

## Common strategies

Use stable, fairly complete fields for blocks: year of birth, sex, postcode prefix, or a phonetic name key. Multi-pass blocking is often safer than a single narrow rule.

## The cost of blocks that are too tight

If a true match fails the block, it never reaches the scoring stage.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
people_a <- 1000
people_b <- 1000
full_pairs <- people_a * people_b
blocked_pairs <- people_a * 8
c(full_pairs = full_pairs, blocked_pairs = blocked_pairs)
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
   full_pairs blocked_pairs 
        1e+06         8e+03 
```


:::
:::


A good block cuts the search space sharply without discarding plausible matches.
